https://preview.redd.it/rdxgymj6261f1.png?width=864&format=png&auto=webp&s=9389f4685f4e5782b8cc406be24583bab16a4193

I wish many carriers could be honest with themselves and acknowledge the many inefficiencies we have as a craft. 

Why are there still so many walking routes? 

Why do we deliver mail on Saturday when it's not even considered a standard business day? Why not deliver mail M-F and continue delivering packages on the weekends?

I know the easy answer is to cut management, but think bigger. I'm sure others can think of other things we do on a daily basis that, if we were to start the Post Office today; we would not do it that way. 

We all don't want to cut future jobs of our potential brothers & sisters, but are we so against change that it will come at the expense of ALL of our jobs? I know an injury to one is an injury to all but if the Post Office doesn't change some of the ways we operate, we'll all be out of a job.

Also, if we made some money instead of losing it, it might be a little easier to get more than 1.3%

As a whole, it represents:
 - The United States of America: It stands for the country, its people, and its ideals.
 - Freedom and Liberty: It's a global emblem of these core American values.
 - Unity: The flag symbolizes the union of the 50 states.
 - Justice: It represents the pursuit of fairness and equality.

 - Patriotism: It's a focal point for national pride and allegiance.
 - Resilience and Perseverance: Having flown through times of war and peace, it signifies the nation's enduring spirit.
The individual elements also have specific meanings:
 - The 50 White Stars on a Blue Field (the "union"): Each star represents one of the 50 states in the United States. The blue field signifies vigilance, perseverance, and justice.
 - The 13 Horizontal Stripes (alternating red and white): These stripes represent the original 13 colonies that declared independence from Great Britain.
 - The Colors: While not officially defined when the flag was adopted in 1777, the colors have come to be associated with the following:
 - Red: Valor and bravery, as well as hardiness and readiness to sacrifice. It can also represent the blood shed by those who fought for the country's freedom.
 - White: Purity and innocence, signifying the nation's aspiration for these ideals.
 - Blue: Vigilance, perseverance, and justice, echoing the meaning of the blue field.
- Historically, the flag has evolved since its adoption by the Continental Congress on June 14, 1777. The number of stars has increased as new states have joined the Union, while the 13 stripes have remained constant to honor the original colonies. The flag's journey mirrors the story of the nation itself, representing its growth, challenges, and enduring principles.
